answer: We formalize a protocol in which dynamic opportunity-cost bonds constitute a meadow of locked liquidity, utilizing subgame-perfect punishment matrices to prune adversarial branching. Integrating a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function as a computational lantern ensures that staking collateral costs robustly outpace the garden of aggregate payoffs. Consequently, the expected utility of Sybil multiplication remains strictly negative, establishing a Nash equilibrium wherein honest signaling is the unique dominant strategy.
